text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

--Far-left opposition Socialist Peoples Party (SF) leader Holger Nielsen announced that he was leaning towards recommending a 'no' to the EU Amsterdam treaty reforms in Denmark's referendum to be held in 1998. The party is deeply split on Amsterdam with leading figures supporting the reforms in defiance of Nielsen's 'no'. SF debates its final stance on the issue at a party conference to be held in September. A date for the referendum has not been set yet.

--Danish wind turbine manufacturers can expect annual billion crown turnover until the year 2000 after Danish electricity companies and energy authorities selected four offshore sites where two-three thousand turbines are to be erected.
--Monday night's violent rain and thunder storms in Denmark are expected to cost insurance companies 60-80 million crowns in damage claims.

--Scandinavian Airlines (SAS) reports unchanged passenger traffic in June on its domestic Aalborg(north Jutland)-Copenhagen route despite the opening of the bridge-tunnel rail fixed link over the Great Belt waterway, which has shortened train journey times dramatically. SAS' Aarhus-Copenhagen route posted 1-2 percent lower passenger volume.
--New legislation means that Danish telecommunications group Tele Danmark will have to drastically cut its telephony prices in the coming months.
--Danish industrial hourly wages have reached new world record heights due to the tax system, a German industrial think tank report claims.
--Denmark's Brewery Association is to launch a major new sales campaign for local beer as Danish domestic ale consumption stagnates or falls in favour of soft drinks.
